title: Hierarchical Transformation of Navigational Variables into Coordinated Turning
source_locator: Fig. 2c (DNa02>SPARC2-D-CsChrimson, Unilateral group); Fig. S3; Results 'LAL013 interfaces with a hierarchical network of descending neurons'
quote: Turns induced by DNa02 activation were weakest, typically below 50°/s and highly probabilistic, consistent with previous reports8,9 (Fig. 2c and Fig. S3).
mapping_basis: The paper names the neuron DNa02, a Namiki/MANC type name listed in type_list.csv; its driver (R75C10-AD; R87D07-DBD = SS00730 per Fig. S3/S4 and Supplementary Table 1) maps to DNa02 in driver_lines.csv.
stimulation: 660 nm fibre-coupled laser, ~0.73 mW/mm2, 5 s constant light per session, 10 sessions per fly
type_coverage: stochastic: left, right, both or neither DNa02 labelled, scored post hoc; this record is the unilateral group
sensory_condition: tethered on air-suspended spherical treadmill, very dim ambient light
other_cell_types: unnamed off-target cells co-labelled by the DNa02 driver (Fig. S4f legend)
coordination_notes: weak ipsilateral turns; only ball angular velocity reported for DNa02, no leg tracking
penetrance: highly probabilistic; unilateral vs no label p<0.01 (Fig. 2c)
notes: Flies were placed to walk on the ball and the outcome is ball angular velocity only, so per PROTOCOL 3 (turning in walking flies) leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed; no stepping, leg kinematics or standing-fly data are reported for DNa02. Sex: genotype 'nSyb-PhiC31 in attP18 / w' (Supplementary Table 1) has two X chromosomes, and Methods say mostly females were used. Other DNa02 experiments in this paper (GtACR2 epistasis Fig. 2e-g, reaper/grim ablation Fig. 3/S4, imaging Fig. 5/S7/S8) are not activation and give no records.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior'; Figure 8A-C (unilateral ReaChR); Methods 'Stochastic ReaChR expression'
quote: In the flies with unilateral expression, we found that light evoked a small average steering bias in the ipsilateral direction
mapping_basis: The paper names the neuron DNa02, a Namiki/MANC type name listed in type_list.csv; Methods state ReaChR was driven by the DNa02 split-Gal4 line SS00730, which driver_lines.csv maps to DNa02.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric on both sides, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s on every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: stochastic; this record is flies with one DNa02 expressing ReaChR (scored post hoc by dissection)
sensory_condition: on air-supported spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact, no dissection before behaviour
other_cell_types: unnamed off-target optic lobe cell types
coordination_notes: only ball rotational velocity measured; legs not tracked in this experiment
penetrance: small mean ipsilateral bias (peak ~50 deg/s), outside 95% CI of bootstrap null from bilateral siblings; individual flies variable (Fig. 8C)
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: 16 unilateral flies; Methods count 17 unilateral brains (9 left-only, 8 right-only) of 73 experiments
notes: Flies were walking on the treadmill when illuminated; the outcome is a steering bias, so leg-rhythm fields are not_assessed (PROTOCOL 3). Forward-velocity changes were attributed to visual startle by the authors. The 'simulation' in the text is a bootstrap resampling of control flies, not a connectome model. Leg kinematics in this paper (Fig. 8F-H) come from GtACR1 silencing, not activation. Other CsChrimson uses (Fig. 5) activate ORNs or antennal thermoreceptors, not DNs. Off-target expression from the Figure 8-figure supplement 2 legend.

title: Neural circuit mechanisms for steering control in walking Drosophila
source_locator: Results 'Contributions of single descending neuron types to steering behavior' (paragraph after Figure 8 supplements); Figure 8B-C (bilateral ReaChR group)
quote: These effects were likely due to visual startle, because they were indistinguishable in flies with unilateral expression, bilateral expression, and no expression (data not shown).
mapping_basis: The paper names the neuron DNa02, a Namiki/MANC type name listed in type_list.csv; Methods state ReaChR was driven by SS00730, which driver_lines.csv maps to DNa02.
stimulation: 617 nm orange light from above the head, symmetric on both sides, 68 uW/mm2, 0.5 s on every 11 s, 150 trials
type_coverage: stochastic; this record is flies with both DNa02 neurons expressing ReaChR
sensory_condition: on air-supported spherical treadmill; head cuticle intact, no dissection before behaviour
other_cell_types: unnamed off-target optic lobe cell types
n_flies_note: Fig. 8B legend: 17 bilateral flies; Methods report 47 brains with bilateral expression
notes: Bilateral-expression siblings were used only as the null control. Their signed 'ipsilateral' rotation is zero by construction (random left/right labels), so it says nothing about turning. Forward-velocity changes matched no-expression flies, and the authors say they could not use the dataset to judge DNa02's effect on forward velocity. So no DNa02-specific walking outcome can be coded. Kept as a record because DNa02 was bilaterally activated in walking flies with ball tracking; every outcome field is not_assessed.
